channel_name: This Week in Startups · Jason Calacanis
video_title: Cedric the Entertainer Judges Qloo’s AI Hackathon Finale | E2367
gist: TWiST hackathon finale for Qloo (auto-captioned as 'Clue'), Jason Calacanis's taste-intelligence portfolio company, which pitches its taste knowledge graph as a deterministic 'service primitive' for consumer AI agents. Cedric the Entertainer, Calacanis, Qloo's CEO and co-host Lon judge three Qloo-powered apps: Undertoe (taste-based county vote prediction and ad-spend targeting, which won), Backline (agentic travel planning with a built-in wallet) and Roomful (taste-generated VR relaxation spaces).

themes.theme: Qloo as taste layer for agentic AI

insights.claim: Qloo (transcribed as 'Clue'), a 15-year-old taste-intelligence company, positions its knowledge graphs/ontologies spanning POIs, restaurants, music, film and consumer brands as an API primitive that gives developers and enterprises the kind of taste data Spotify, Netflix or Expedia keep in-house.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Taste/preference data offered as an open API is a picks-and-shovels play on consumer AI agents; watch Qloo as a private-market comp for data-layer businesses.
insights.quote: we basically have developed kind of some of the deepest knowledge graphs and ontologies about taste

insights.claim: Qloo's CEO argues the key missing gap for consumer AI agents that shop and act on a person's behalf is understanding who the user is and their taste, framing Qloo as a 'service primitive' in the agentic AI stack.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Personalization/identity-of-taste is a candidate bottleneck layer in agentic commerce; companies owning proprietary preference graphs may capture value as agents proliferate.
insights.quote: you could kind of think of Clue as like a service primitive in the kind of agentic AI stack

insights.claim: Qloo pitches its output as deterministic, which it says appeals to agent builders trying to lower inference cost and needing a 'grounding' layer; it says agent-travel startups have approached it for this.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Deterministic structured data that substitutes for LLM inference calls is a cost-reduction pitch to watch as agent margins tighten.
insights.quote: Everyone's trying to lower the cost of inference and so clue is deterministic

insights.claim: Qloo says some of its biggest customers are in travel, naming Michelin, Tablet Hotels and AmEx.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Travel/hospitality is the leading enterprise buyer of taste-personalization data, signaling where AI personalization budgets are flowing first.
insights.quote: Some of our biggest customers are all in the travel space

insights.claim: Jason Calacanis frames Qloo as one of his earliest angel investments that started roughly 10 years before ChatGPT and survived long enough for the AI wave to arrive, an example of a pre-LLM data company becoming newly relevant.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Pre-LLM companies with proprietary structured datasets can see renewed relevance and valuation in the AI cycle; screen older data-asset startups for this re-rating.

insights.claim: Qloo's hackathon run with Devpost drew nearly 3,000 participants, with submissions spanning game-world localization, portable taste profiles, architecture-as-a-service, empty-storefront ideation and nonverbal communication aids.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Large developer turnout signals building interest in taste APIs for agents; developer-ecosystem breadth is a leading indicator for API businesses.

insights.claim: Hackathon winner Undertoe maps Qloo heat maps for 77 tastes onto every US county and uses a regression on the strongest 24 to predict county-level 2024 votes; it claims to have correctly called Michigan and Wisconsin where polls missed.
insights.speaker: Abdal Hassani (Undertoe founder)
insights.so_what: Consumer-taste data as an alternative signal to polling could become a product for campaigns and pollsters; treat the backtest claim as unaudited.
insights.quote: We pulled clue heat maps for 77 tastes and mapped them onto every county

insights.claim: Undertoe claims a polls-plus-Qloo blend, run before the midterm results, called 32 of 33 states correctly versus 31 for betting markets and poll-based forecasts alone, including correctly predicting Iowa going blue.
insights.speaker: Abdal Hassani (Undertoe founder)
insights.so_what: A one-state edge over prediction markets is a thin but notable sign that alternative consumer data could add signal to election forecasting and prediction-market pricing.
insights.quote: our polls plus uh clue blend predicted 32 out of 33 states right correctly whereas betting markets and polls based forecasts alone predicted 31

insights.claim: Undertoe's agent allocates campaign ad spend zip by zip using taste signals; e.g., it flagged Warren County, Iowa as leaning +2 Democrat by tastes versus roughly R+7 in polls, identifying it as a persuasion target.
insights.speaker: Abdal Hassani (Undertoe founder)
insights.so_what: Taste-vs-poll divergence as a targeting signal is a framework applicable beyond politics to any geo-targeted ad budget.

insights.claim: Calacanis picked Undertoe as his top investment choice because political campaign spending recurs every two years and peaks every four, giving it the clearest monetization path, especially if plugged into ad networks like Facebook, Google or TikTok ads.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Cyclical political ad budgets are a reliable revenue pool for ad-tech/data startups; integration with major ad networks is the distribution unlock.
insights.quote: I think that one has the clearest path to being a business

insights.claim: Qloo's CEO and Cedric see Undertoe as dual-use: the same localized taste targeting could serve artists' managers planning ad spend, touring comedians or bands tailoring set lists, outside election cycles.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO) / Cedric the Entertainer
insights.so_what: The non-election use case determines whether a political-data startup smooths its revenue cycle; diligence should probe off-cycle demand.

insights.claim: Qloo's CEO argues that getting users to delegate spending (not just calendar or workflow tasks) to an AI agent is the 'final frontier' of trust, and that capturing travel & entertainment spend via agents is a $100B+ opportunity.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Agent payments/delegated commerce in travel is a large prize; watch who solves trust and personalization in agent-booked travel.
insights.quote: to actually delegate spend is kind of the final frontier

insights.claim: The AI travel-agent space is described by the judges as very crowded because the prize is so large, making differentiation the key question for entrants like Backline.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO) / Lon (TWiST co-host)
insights.so_what: Crowded AI travel agent category implies weak moats for undifferentiated apps; favor players with proprietary data or payments integration.
insights.quote: it's a crowded space in the agent realm and for good reason

insights.claim: Backline is a travel-planning agent that builds a taste-personalized itinerary from a prompt and budget using Qloo, prices real flights, includes a built-in wallet to pay for flights, hotels and restaurants, uses agents to make reservations autonomously, and offers 3D previews of destinations.
insights.speaker: Josiah Oluadare (Backline founder)
insights.so_what: Bundling itinerary, payment wallet and autonomous booking is the emerging template for agentic travel products.
insights.quote: It also has agent built in the back end that can make reservations for you

insights.claim: Lon says most AI itinerary apps he has seen produce poor, generic plans that misread the user, so a travel app that truly nails taste-based itineraries would be a 'miracle app' with broad demand.
insights.speaker: Lon (TWiST co-host)
insights.so_what: Personalization quality, not booking capability, is the current failure point of AI travel apps; that is where an edge can be built.

insights.claim: Cedric highlights group trips with mixed budgets (from a billionaire to a postal worker in the same group) as an unsolved travel-planning pain point a taste-plus-budget agent could address, along with 'high-low' itineraries mixing luxury hotels with local spots.
insights.speaker: Cedric the Entertainer
insights.so_what: Multi-budget group trip planning is a concrete underserved feature that could differentiate a travel agent product.

insights.claim: Roomful (from Shrewzy) generates a taste-based relaxing environment with music via Qloo's API and lets users walk inside it via a world model/VR; its founder proposes a monthly subscription aimed at burnt-out Gen Z and solo founders seeking affordable escape.
insights.speaker: Tiwa Bakray (Roomful founder)
insights.so_what: Consumer VR wellness subscriptions remain an unproven business; the judges saw creativity but unclear monetization.

insights.claim: Calacanis cites his early angel bet on Calm, which started by selling a meditation subscription to about 100 people for $10 a year and became worth hundreds of millions of dollars, as proof that meditation apps can be big businesses, though he calls the market possibly flooded.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Meditation/wellness subscriptions can scale massively from tiny starts, but category saturation raises the bar for new entrants.
insights.quote: There is uh a market for meditation apps. It might be a little flooded

insights.claim: Qloo's CEO sees Roomful as a dark horse better suited as a Pinterest-like interior décor/design tool than a meditation app.
insights.speaker: Alex (Qloo CEO)
insights.so_what: Pivoting taste-driven generative spaces toward interior design could tap clearer commercial intent than wellness.
insights.quote: it could actually be kind of a dark horse

insights.claim: Final judging: Undertoe won with 7 points, Backline was second with 6, Roomful third with 5; the $25,000 cash pool split $15,000/$6,000/$4,000, and Calacanis separately offered a $25K investment prize contingent on founders committing to work on the company for at least six months after due diligence.
insights.speaker: Lon (TWiST co-host) / Alex (Qloo CEO) / Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Undertoe is the likely recipient of Calacanis's follow-on capital; it is an early-stage name to track in political ad-tech.
